Hi Samir — thanks for the detailed list and for joining the demo. Appreciate the usage context; that helps. High-level answers and an initial sketch attached (redwood_obs_pricing_v1.xlsx):

- Retention tiers: we price observability storage as a combination of hot storage (ingest + queryable retention) and cold archived snapshots. Hot is metered per-GB/month; archived traces are billed at a separate archival rate (roughly 20% of hot per-GB/month) and do not count against hot query SLA unless restored. For your 15TB/month ramp, we typically recommend a hybrid approach (first 2 months hot, then archive partitions weekly).

- Tracing: charged by ingest volume (GB of spans) rather than raw sampled span counts; this is more predictable for billing. For deterministic sampling we can apply an "inbound-sampling" discount (we reduce billable ingest by the sampling factor) — typical concession is 10-25% depending on visibility needs.

- Dashboards: advanced dashboard add-on is billed per-seat for editors and per-org for viewers. Advanced widgets (heavy aggregation, long-window joins) carry a small per-seat surcharge; we can offer a seat-bundle (10 seats) at a flat rate if you expect a larger authoring team.

- Credits/commit: we do offer usage-credit commitments for Year 1 to smooth onboarding spikes. Example path in workbook: 12-month commit with a 20% upfront usage credit applied during the first 3 months, then tapering credits months 4-6. Alternatively, a 6-mo pilot with higher credits is possible.

- SLA & storage: retention SLO for hot storage is 99.9%, archived snapshots are stored in region of choice with optional cross-region replication (additional fee).

Next steps: I flagged a suggested two-track offer in the spreadsheet — (A) 12-month commit + usage credit curve, (B) 6-month pilot + larger short-term credit. Can you confirm the expected monthly max ingest (GB) and whether deterministic sampling is in place?

Attachments: redwood_obs_pricing_v1.xlsx (pricing scenarios). HubSpot record: https://hubspot.com/deals/DC-2026-0921
